sports.h3: National Bank Open in full swing across Montreal and Toronto
sports.summary: The Canadian hard court double is underway with the men in Montreal and women in Toronto, though several headliners are sitting this one out.
body: The 2026 National Bank Open is deep into its opening rounds this week, running from August 1 through the finals on August 13. The men play the Masters 1000 event at IGA Stadium in Montreal while the women contest the WTA 1000 at Sobeys Stadium in Toronto.

World number one Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic both opted to skip Montreal, thinning the top of the men's draw and opening a path for the next tier of contenders. Tuesday's Montreal order of play featured names like Draper, Hurkacz, Cerundolo and Monfils working through the early rounds.
The expanded two week format gives players extra rest days before the Cincinnati swing and the US Open series ramps up later in the month.

sports.h3: Gauff tops Toronto field as Andreescu draws Krejcikova
sports.summary: Coco Gauff leads the WTA Canadian Open draw in Toronto, where two former Slam champions meet in an early blockbuster.
body: The WTA 1000 in Toronto features a stacked field led by Aryna Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff at the top of the seeding. Mirra Andreeva, Linda Noskova, Iga Swiatek and Amanda Anisimova round out the top eight.
One of the early standout matchups pits home favourite Bianca Andreescu against two time major winner Barbora Krejcikova, a first round clash of Slam champions that would headline most tournaments.
Filipino breakout star Alex Eala earned a seeding boost after a strong run of results, underlining how quickly the WTA pecking order is shifting this season.

sports.h3: Alcaraz cleared to return and eyeing Cincinnati comeback
sports.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has been given the all clear after a wrist injury and is targeting the Cincinnati Masters for his return.
body: Doctors have confirmed that Alcaraz's right wrist has fully recovered from the severe tenosynovitis that flared in mid April. The injury forced him to miss the French Open, Wimbledon and Montreal, a brutal stretch of lost points at his best surfaces.
The Spaniard is skipping the Canadian swing but plans to reappear at the Cincinnati Masters, giving himself a hard court tune up ahead of the US Open.
His absence has let Sinner stretch a commanding lead atop the rankings, so Alcaraz returns with plenty to chase in the back half of the season.

sports.h3: Sinner's relentless run pads his lead at the top
sports.summary: Jannik Sinner heads into August as world number one after a second straight Wimbledon title and a near flawless first half.
body: Sinner has won six of the seven biggest events since early February, becoming the first player to sweep the opening five Masters 1000 titles of a season at Indian Wells, Miami, Monte Carlo, Madrid and Rome.
That completed his Career Golden Masters and, paired with a second consecutive Wimbledon crown, pushed him past Alcaraz in their ongoing big title battle.
With Alcaraz sidelined for much of the clay and grass swing, Sinner enters the North American hard courts as the clear favourite to keep the number one ranking through the US Open.

sports.h3: ADCC World Championship heads to Krakow for the first time
sports.summary: The 2026 ADCC World Championship will be held at Tauron Arena in Krakow, Poland, marking the country's first time hosting the sport's biggest no gi event.
body: ADCC has confirmed its flagship World Championship for September 12 and 13 at the 15,000 seat Tauron Arena Krakow. It is the first time Poland has staged the event and the first Worlds since Las Vegas in 2024.

The best submission grapplers on the planet, including reigning champions, trials winners and elite invitees, will fight for the most prestigious title in no gi grappling. The event streams exclusively on FloSports.
With qualification wrapping up through the trials system, the athlete list is nearly locked as the countdown to Krakow begins.

sports.h3: Gordon Ryan rules himself out of ADCC 2026
sports.summary: The dominant no gi star Gordon Ryan says he will not compete at the 2026 ADCC World Championship, leaving the superheavyweight picture wide open.
body: Ryan, long regarded as the most feared grappler in the sport, has stated he is not returning for ADCC 2026. Persistent health issues have limited his competitive schedule over the past two years.
His absence removes the biggest name from the Krakow card and hands a genuine opening to a new generation of heavyweights who have spent years chasing him.
The vacuum sets up one of the most unpredictable ADCC brackets in recent memory as contenders jockey for the crown he leaves behind.

sports.h3: Baku set to stage the 2026 World Judo Championships
sports.summary: The IJF World Judo Championships return to Baku, Azerbaijan this autumn, the pinnacle of the judo calendar on the road to Los Angeles 2028.
body: Azerbaijan's capital will host the Worlds from October 4 to 11, the second time Baku has staged the event after 2018. The program features 15 events across seven men's, seven women's and one mixed team category.
IJF President Marius Vizer praised Baku's track record, calling it a guarantee of a top level event both on the tatami and in its organisation.
The championships offer crucial world ranking points as athletes begin positioning themselves for Olympic qualification in the new cycle.

sports.h3: Spain close on Australia as SailGP breaks before Germany
sports.summary: Spain has narrowed the gap to Australia's Flying Roos in the SailGP championship, with Artemis climbing to third after Portsmouth.
body: Following the Great Britain Sail Grand Prix in Portsmouth in late July, Spain inched closer to the series leading Bonds Flying Roos while the Swiss backed Artemis team surged into third overall.
Artemis sit on 47 points, just one ahead of the United States, underlining how tightly packed the chasing pack has become. Australia remain the red hot favourites to take the title.
The fleet now waits for the ROCKWOOL Germany Sail Grand Prix in Sassnitz on August 22 and 23, the next chance to shake up the standings.

sports.h3: Norris grabs Hungary win as F1 heads into summer break
sports.summary: Lando Norris took his first victory of 2026 at the Hungarian Grand Prix, the last race before Formula 1's three week shutdown.
body: Norris lost the lead to teammate Oscar Piastri off the line but reclaimed it after the second round of pit stops, then held on ahead of Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli. Piastri retired from second with a gearbox failure.
It was Norris's first win as reigning world champion at a circuit he has now won at more than once. The result took some pressure off after a mixed run of form.
Kimi Antonelli extended his championship lead heading into the break, with the season set to resume at a sprint weekend for the Dutch Grand Prix from August 21 to 23.

sports.h3: Verstappen future dominates F1 silly season
sports.summary: Max Verstappen's contract has become the central storyline of the driver market as reports swirl over his Red Bull commitment.
body: Verstappen holds a Red Bull deal through 2028, but a performance clause could let him leave at the end of this year if he was not in the top two of the standings by the summer break. A difficult first half has left him well outside that mark.
Jos Verstappen has bluntly rejected Dutch reports that his son is preparing to recommit to Red Bull for 2027 while negotiating a richer contract without an exit clause.
Red Bull is reportedly willing to raise the four time champion's salary in exchange for removing the clause, a saga that could trigger a chain of moves across the grid.

sports.h3: Eredivisie kicks off Friday with Cambuur against Excelsior
sports.summary: The new Dutch top flight season starts this Friday, with three time defending champions PSV opening at home.
body: The 2026-27 Eredivisie runs from August 7 through late May, with SC Cambuur and Excelsior Rotterdam opening the campaign on Friday evening in Leeuwarden.
Defending champions PSV begin their title defence at home against Fortuna Sittard, while Ajax travel to PEC Zwolle in the same time slot.
The traditional powers reshaped their squads over the summer, setting up what looks like a genuinely open race after PSV's recent grip on the trophy.

sports.h3: Ajax bolster attack with Marcos Leonardo signing
sports.summary: Ajax have added firepower under manager Michel, landing striker Marcos Leonardo from Al-Hilal as they chase domestic dominance.
body: Ajax have been busy in the market this summer, with the arrival of Marcos Leonardo from Al-Hilal the marquee move to strengthen their frontline. The Brazilian gives Michel a proven goal threat.
The Amsterdam club are determined to reclaim the title after ceding ground to PSV in recent seasons and have overhauled the squad accordingly.
With PSV, Feyenoord and Ajax all reshaping their rosters, previews point to one of the most competitive Dutch title races in years.

consumer-tech.h3: Google locks in August 12 for Pixel 11 launch
consumer-tech.summary: Google will unveil the Pixel 11 lineup and Pixel Watch 5 at a Made by Google event on August 12, moving the keynote to prime time.
body: Google has confirmed its next Made by Google event for August 12 at 6 PM ET in New York, ditching the usual midday slot for an evening show. The invite teased a gold phone with a glowing camera bar.

The Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL and 11 Pro Fold are all expected, powered by the new Tensor G6 chip, alongside the Tensor driven Pixel Watch 5. Leaks point to a brighter Samsung OLED panel, 256GB base storage across the range and a possible price bump.
The event streams live on Google's Made by Google YouTube channel, kicking off the busiest stretch of the fall phone season.

consumer-tech.h3: Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra lands with a brighter, bigger screen
consumer-tech.summary: Samsung's flagship foldable goes on sale this week with an 8 inch inner display and a 200MP camera, though reviewers flag the higher price.
body: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra pairs an 8 inch LTPO AMOLED inner screen at 120Hz and 3,000 nits with a 6.5 inch cover display, a 200MP main camera and a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip. The hinge slims down to 4.1mm unfolded.
Early reviews praise the brighter, less reflective display and the best battery life of any Galaxy foldable so far, but note a weak telephoto lens, no S Pen support and only minor design changes.
Pricing starts at 2,099 dollars for 256GB, a 100 dollar jump over last year, with sales beginning August 7.

consumer-tech.h3: Samsung Unpacked delivered foldables, watches and glasses
consumer-tech.summary: Samsung's July Unpacked event rolled out the Z Fold 8 series, the Z Flip 8, new Galaxy Watches and its first Galaxy smart glasses.
body: At its summer Unpacked, Samsung introduced a reworked Z Fold 8 with more passport like proportions plus the Z Fold 8 Ultra, the Z Flip 8 and refreshed Galaxy Watch models.
The headline surprise was Galaxy Glasses, Samsung's entry into the AI smart eyewear race that Meta and Google are also chasing hard.
The lineup signals Samsung's push to spread beyond phones into wearables and face worn computing as the next battleground.

consumer-tech.h3: Meta widens its AI glasses lead with 299 dollar frames
consumer-tech.summary: Meta rolled out three new AI glasses starting at 299 dollars, undercutting its own previous models as rivals close in.
body: Meta launched the Adventurer, Fury and a Kylie Jenner branded model, all matching Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2 specs but costing 80 dollars less. The frames now carry Meta's own brand for the first time.
Every model ships with Muse Spark, Meta's first proprietary AI model built specifically for on device wearable inference. The Kylie edition adds an AI generated voice assistant for 399 dollars.
Meta holds roughly 80 percent of the AI smart glasses market and the aggressive pricing is a clear move to defend that lead as Google and Samsung push in.

consumer-tech.h3: Bose readies a second generation QuietComfort
consumer-tech.summary: Leaks point to a new Bose QuietComfort with lossless USB-C audio and a refreshed design arriving in mid August.
body: A second generation Bose QuietComfort is expected to launch around August 13 at 359 dollars, adding lossless USB-C audio, TrueSpatial spatial sound and a redesigned build.
Bose is leaning on its strengths in comfort and low frequency noise cancellation, while the current QuietComfort model has already slid to 229 dollars ahead of the successor.
The refresh keeps Bose competitive against Sony's flagship over ear cans, which counter with longer battery life and LDAC support.

consumer-tech.h3: OpenAI expands GPT-5.6 family and sunsets o3
consumer-tech.summary: OpenAI's new GPT-5.6 model family is rolling out broadly while the older o3 model is scheduled for retirement later in August.
body: OpenAI launched the GPT-5.6 family in July, led by the flagship Sol alongside the balanced Terra and cost efficient Luna. It also introduced GPT-Live voice models that can listen and speak at the same time.
Late July brought steep price cuts, with GPT-5.6 Luna dropping 80 percent and Terra 20 percent as OpenAI pushes for wider adoption.
As part of the transition, the o3 model will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26 following a 90 day sunset period.

consumer-tech.h3: Windows 11 August update lets you uninstall an AI model
consumer-tech.summary: Microsoft's August update adds the first ability to remove a built in AI component, plus new sign in security and touchpad gestures.
body: The Windows 11 August update, expected on Patch Tuesday around August 11, lets users uninstall the Image Generation AI model through Settings for the first time. Users still cannot strip out all AI features at once.
The release also brings Windows Hello Enhanced Sign-in Security for external fingerprint sensors, new touchpad gestures, Voice Isolation for Voice Access and Fluid Dictation for Voice Typing.
Microsoft is framing the update around reliability, with a smarter search index, a more stable File Explorer and a raft of performance fixes rather than flashy new looks.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple ships iOS 26.6 with heavy security patching
consumer-tech.summary: Apple's iOS 26.6 and its companion updates landed with over 80 security fixes and Spotlight tuning ahead of iOS 27.
body: iOS 26.6, macOS Tahoe 26.6, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS 26.6 arrived with more than 80 security fixes and optimizations to the Spotlight index that underpins Siri and search.
The 26 cycle introduced the Liquid Glass redesign, the biggest visual overhaul since iOS 7, plus live translation, AI powered shortcuts and updated Visual Intelligence.
This is likely the last incremental release before iOS 27, and Apple is nudging users to update now since the coming AI features will lean heavily on the Spotlight index.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla's next Roadster set to break cover this month
consumer-tech.summary: Tesla has scheduled the long delayed second generation Roadster to finally debut in August, promising a sub one second sprint.
body: After years of delays, the next generation Tesla Roadster is slated to be revealed in August. Tesla has hyped it as the most radical electric sports car on the market.
The company claims aerospace derived technology and a sub one second zero to sixty time, figures that would put it in a class of its own if they hold up in production.
A credible reveal would be a rare bright spot for Tesla's product narrative as rivals crowd into the mainstream EV space.

consumer-tech.h3: Rivian's R2 pushes the brand toward the mainstream
consumer-tech.summary: Rivian has begun customer deliveries of its cheaper R2 SUV, its big bet to grow from a niche maker into a mass market name.
body: Rivian's R2 is meant to transform the company from a luxury EV niche player into a mainstream brand. The first trim to ship is the 57,990 dollar Performance with 656 horsepower and a 3.6 second zero to sixty.

A 53,990 dollar Premium version arrives late this year with up to 330 miles of EPA estimated range. CEO RJ Scaringe says the R2 will compete not just with Tesla but with legacy names like Jeep and Subaru.
Rivian's production targets for the R2 remain ambitious, and hitting them is central to the automaker's path to profitability.

consumer-tech.h3: NACS rollout reshapes EV charging in 2026
consumer-tech.summary: The shift to Tesla's charging standard and wider Supercharger access is making 2026 a turning point for charging convenience.
body: Ford, GM, Rivian, Volvo, Mercedes-Benz, Hyundai, Kia and others have adopted Tesla's North American Charging Standard, and adapters that let non Tesla vehicles use Superchargers are now rolling out in volume.
The change opens thousands of reliable fast charging stalls to a much larger pool of drivers, easing one of the biggest pain points for EV adoption.
Automakers are also extending charging perks, with Ford renewing its Power Promise program nearly two years after launch.

consumer-tech.summary: Vehicle to grid and vehicle to home charging are lining up across cars, hardware and utilities as BYD pushes ultra fast charging.
body: Bidirectional charging is coming together on three fronts at once with more capable vehicles, more home hardware and more utility support. Owners of eligible Ford, GM, Hyundai, Kia, Tesla and Nissan EVs are starting to see value beyond range.
Volkswagen is launching a fully integrated vehicle to grid offer for private customers in Germany, with more European countries to follow, since its ID family has been bidirectional ready since 2023.
On the charging speed side, BYD says its Flash Chargers can deliver up to 1,500 kilowatts to cars fitted with its latest Blade Battery.
